title: First look at the evaluation of two-loop Feynman integrals for radiative return processes
description: 2-loop planar 4-point double box with electron mass on 6 lines, off-shell leg q^2; contains the nested-square-root kite sector and 2 elliptic sectors; 68 MIs [Euclidean fallback point]
mapping_notes: All p incoming, p1+p2+p3+p4=0. Independent p1,p2,p3: p1^2=p2^2=m2, p3^2=0, p1.p2=(s-2m2)/2, p2.p3=(t-m2)/2, p1.p3=(u-m2)/2 with u=2m2+q2-s-t. D1..D9 order kept (D8,D9 auxiliary). PHYSICAL boundary point x0 eq.(64) (s=16 GeV^2, m_e^2 ~2.6e-7: extreme hierarchy, s-channel above all thresholds); no causal object (derived contour). Euclidean fallback <slug>_euclid.json at m2=1,s=-3,t=-2,u=-1 (q2=-8), all F coefficients positive.

point.note: Euclidean fallback point (all F coefficients positive). The paper only quotes values at paper_point, a physical point where DiffExp 2.2 cannot yet derive every causal side, so reference_values are not compared here.

normalization: Paper eq.(6): FFG = e^{2 eps gamma_E} (m^2)^{2eps - a} prod d^Dk/(i pi^{D/2}) prod 1/D_i^{a_i}, a=sum a_i, D=q^2-m^2 (+i delta). So FFG = e^{2eps gamma_E} (m2)^{2eps-a} (-1)^a J_DiffExp. a=7 for [1^7,0,0], a=6 for the ISP ones. DiffExp FT: denominators D=m^2-q^2 (Euclidean-positive), measure prod d^dk/(i pi^{d/2}), no exp(L eps gamma_E) (see de22/docs/amflow-comparison.md, feynman-families.md). Paper Minkowski integral with (q^2-m^2+i0) denominators = (-1)^{sum nu} * DiffExp value (numerator powers included in sum nu).
confidence: high for family; medium for M3 mapping and for physical-point feasibility.
